source.paper: Schulman, Wolski, Dhariwal, Radford, Klimov. Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms. arXiv:1707.06347v2
source.cross_checked_in: PPO reading notes in the course workspace (PPO_论文精读_arXiv1707.06347.md, section 8.1): the full 11-row table

paper_metric: average normalised score over 7 MuJoCo tasks (-v1), 1,000,000 steps per run, 3 seeds, scored on the last 100 episodes; the paper reports one aggregate number per setting, without variance
paper_normalisation: per-task shift-and-scale with a random policy = 0 and the best result = 1, then averaged over 21 runs; the reference scores behind that scaling are not published
notes: The paper's overall winner is eps = 0.2 (0.82) and its worst setting is no clipping (-0.39, below the random-policy anchor).
d_targ = 0.01 is the paper's best adaptive-KL setting, which is why the C1 KL arm re-implements that one.
The paper reports no std or confidence interval, so 0.82 vs 0.74 carries no published significance claim; our 3-seed mean +- std is a contribution beyond the original.
Our runs use 3 of the 7 tasks (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d) and modern Gymnasium v4 environments, so the aggregate is a 3-task subset, not the paper's 7-task average.
